bull.argument: The filing shows a business growing at a pace that is hard to ignore. Total net sales rose 15% to $478,834 million in 2026, iPhone revenue climbed 21%, and Services grew 13% to $123,301 million. Total gross margin percentage expanded to 48.8% from 46.9%, and products gross margin rose to 39.3%. Demand is broad: Americas, Europe, Greater China and Rest of Asia Pacific all grew. Management is also returning substantial capital, repurchasing $85.8 billion of stock in 2026 and raising the quarterly dividend to $0.27. Liquidity of $136.9 billion is cited as sufficient for cash needs over the next 12 months and beyond. The risks are real: the filing warns of memory and storage cost pressure, tariffs, and litigation affecting App Store commissions. Yet the reported results show the company absorbing these pressures while still expanding margins and revenue. That combination of scale, pricing power, and a Services line growing alongside hardware supports a strong investment case.

claims.claim: Total net sales grew 15% in 2026, with iPhone up 21%.
Total gross margin percentage improved to 48.8% from 46.9%, despite cost pressures.
The company repurchased $85.8 billion of stock and paid $15.7 billion in dividends during 2026.
claims.quote: During 2026, the Company repurchased $85.8 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $15.7 billion.

bear.argument: The bull case rests on reported growth, but the filing signals that the drivers behind that growth are fragile. Products gross margin rose partly because of "tariff refunds," a one-time-type benefit tied to a Supreme Court ruling that the filing says could be reversed: "If tariffs are subsequently rescinded or revoked, the Company may not be able to successfully claim and collect tariff refunds." Meanwhile, R&D jumped 32% to $45,765 million, and the company says the AI investments "may not enhance the Company's products or services or be beneficial or profitable." Component costs are rising, and management expects memory and storage pressure to "intensify." The company also warns that a significant share of its manufacturing is concentrated in Asia and that a single product category drives much of its sales. Strong 2026 results do not remove these exposures, and the filing says gross margins "will be subject to volatility and downward pressure."

claims.claim: Part of the 2026 products margin gain came from tariff refunds, which the filing says may not be collectible if tariffs are revoked.
claims.quote: If tariffs are subsequently rescinded or revoked, the Company may not be able to successfully claim and collect tariff refunds.

claims.claim: Management expects component cost pressure for memory and storage to worsen, threatening future margins.
claims.quote: The Company expects these trends to intensify for memory and storage components.

claims.claim: The filing states the AI investments may not prove profitable, despite the large spending increase.
claims.quote: There are significant risks involved in developing and deploying artificial intelligence and the usage of artificial intelligence may not enhance the Company's products or services or be beneficial or profitable for its business.

bull.argument: The bear case is right that the risks are real, but it overstates how fragile the 2026 results are. Start with tariff refunds: the filing says the Company applied for refunds after a Supreme Court ruling struck down IEEPA tariffs, and that refunds received were recognized as a reduction of products cost of sales. That is a real benefit already booked, not a forecast. The bigger question is whether the core business is weakening, and the filing says it is not. Total net sales grew 15%, Services grew 13% to $123,301 million, and products gross margin rose to 39.3% from 36.8% largely on product mix. R&D's 32% jump is a deliberate investment that management attributes to infrastructure and headcount, and it is being funded by operating results that still expanded margins. The memory and storage pressure is acknowledged, yet it has not stopped revenue or margin expansion. Cash of $136.9 billion and an $85.8 billion buyback in 2026 show the company is funding its risks from strength, not borrowing against them.

claims.claim: Tariff refunds were received and recognized as a reduction of products cost of sales, meaning the benefit is already booked.
claims.quote: has recognized any refunds received as a reduction of products cost of sales

claims.claim: Products gross margin rose primarily due to product mix, not only tariff refunds.
claims.quote: Products gross margin and gross margin percentage increased during 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to product mix and tariff refunds, partially offset by higher costs, including memory.

claims.claim: Management says cash and marketable securities are sufficient for cash requirements over the next 12 months and beyond.
claims.quote: will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond

bear.argument: The bull case treats the 2026 results as proof of durability, but the filing gives reasons to discount them. First, the tariff refunds are real only in the sense that they were booked once; the same filing says "If tariffs are subsequently rescinded or revoked, the Company may not be able to successfully claim and collect tariff refunds," and tariffs remain open under Section 232 and Section 301. A refund-driven lift in products margin is not a repeatable base. Second, the bull points to Services growth, yet the filing describes a concentrated business: it says the Company "generates a significant portion of its net sales from a single product category" and that a Google search licensing arrangement could be disrupted by a reversal of the DOJ case. Third, the buyback of $85.8 billion and the dividend increase are funded while R&D rose 32% and the filing warns "the usage of artificial intelligence may not enhance the Company's products or services or be beneficial or profitable." Strength today does not guarantee returns on spending that is still unproven.

claims.claim: The products margin improvement was partly driven by tariff refunds, and the filing says those refunds may not be collectible if tariffs are revoked.
claims.quote: If tariffs are subsequently rescinded or revoked, the Company may not be able to successfully claim and collect tariff refunds.

claims.claim: The filing says the company depends on one product category for a significant portion of net sales, a concentration that adds risk to the revenue base.
claims.quote: the Company generates a significant portion of its net sales from a single product category

claims.claim: The company warns its AI spending may not prove profitable, even as R&D rose sharply.
claims.quote: the usage of artificial intelligence may not enhance the Company’s products or services or be beneficial or profitable for its business.

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes from the filing, so evidence is comparable. The bull effectively rebuts the tariff-refund concern by noting refunds were already booked and that products margin also rose on mix, though it does not fully address the bear's point that refund-driven gains are non-recurring. The bear answers the bull's strength narrative with concentration and unproven AI spending risks, which the bull only partly engages, so the debate is roughly even.
